items.prompt: Match each simple machine to an example.
pairs: a crowbar lifting a heavy stone
a bucket raised from a well on a rope
a sloping plank for pushing a cart up
hints: Each simple machine makes a job easier in its own way.
Some machines turn, some lift with a rope, and some use a slope or a bar.
Start with the pulley. Think about a rope running over a wheel at the top of a well.
items.explanation: A crowbar is a lever and a well bucket uses a pulley. A sloping plank is a ramp, a bicycle uses gears, and a doorknob is a wheel and axle.

items.prompt: On a seesaw, what is the point in the middle that it turns on called?

options.why: The load is the weight that is being lifted.
The effort is the force you put in.
An axle is the rod in the centre of a wheel.

hints: Every lever turns around one fixed point.
The three lever words are load, effort and pivot.
Cross out the words for the forces.
items.explanation: The pivot, also called the fulcrum, is the fixed point that a lever turns on. On a seesaw, it is the support in the middle.

items.prompt: Dimas uses a long metal bar to lift a heavy rock. The pivot is a small stone near the rock. Where should he push to need the least effort?

options.why: Pushing close to the pivot needs a much bigger effort.

options.text: at the end furthest from the pivot

options.why: The rock is the load. Push on the other end of the bar.

options.text: in the middle of the bar
options.why: That works, but pushing further from the pivot needs even less effort.

hints: Think about opening a heavy door: is it easier to push near the hinges or near the handle?
The hinges of a door act like a pivot.
Compare pushing close to the small stone with pushing far from it.
items.explanation: Pushing at the end furthest from the pivot gives the biggest turning effect, so less effort is needed. This is why long levers make heavy loads easier to lift.

items.prompt: How does a single pulley at the top of a well help you lift a bucket of water?

options.text: It makes the bucket weigh less.
options.why: The bucket's weight does not change. The pulley changes the direction of your pull.

options.text: It lifts the bucket by itself.
options.why: You still have to pull the rope. A machine does not do the work for you.

options.text: It halves the force you need.
options.why: A single fixed pulley does not reduce the force. It only changes its direction.

options.text: It lets you pull down to lift the bucket up, which is easier.

hints: Notice which way you pull the rope and which way the bucket moves.
Pulling down lets you use your own weight to help.
Ask whether a single pulley changes the size of the force or only its direction.
items.explanation: A single fixed pulley changes the direction of your force: you pull down and the bucket goes up. Pulling down is easier because you can use your body weight.

items.prompt: Gear A turns clockwise. Its teeth mesh with the teeth of gear B. Which way does gear B turn?

options.why: Meshing teeth push each other the opposite way.
Gear A's teeth push on gear B's teeth, so gear B must turn.
Gear B turns smoothly in one direction, the opposite way to gear A.

hints: Where the two gears touch, their teeth push each other.
Hold your two fists together like gears and roll them to watch the directions.
Picture the teeth where the gears meet, and follow which way gear A pushes them.
items.explanation: When two gears mesh, the teeth push each other, so the second gear turns the opposite way. Gear B turns anticlockwise.

items.prompt: A big gear with 30 teeth turns a small gear with 10 teeth. When the big gear turns once, how many times does the small gear turn?
hints: Each tooth of the big gear pushes one tooth of the small gear.
One turn of the big gear moves 30 teeth past the small gear.
Work out how many lots of 10 teeth are in 30 teeth.
items.explanation: One turn of the big gear moves 30 teeth, and the small gear needs 10 teeth for one turn. So it turns 30 ÷ 10 = 3 times.

items.prompt: Choose all the tools that use a lever.

options.why: A ramp is an inclined plane. It has no pivot.

options.text: a flagpole rope over a wheel
options.why: A rope over a wheel is a pulley.

hints: A lever is a bar that turns on a pivot.
Look for the pivot in each tool.
Start with scissors. Find the screw that the two blades turn on.
items.explanation: Scissors, bottle openers and wheelbarrows all turn on a pivot, so they are levers. A ramp is an inclined plane, and a flagpole uses a pulley.

items.prompt: A ruler balances on a pivot at its middle. A 6 N weight hangs 20 cm to the left of the pivot. How far to the right must a 4 N weight hang to balance it?
hints: The ruler balances when the turning effect on each side is the same.
Turning effect = force × distance from the pivot.
Work out the turning effect on the left first: 6 N × 20 cm.
items.explanation: The left side has a turning effect of 6 × 20 = 120. The right side needs 4 × distance = 120, so the distance is 120 ÷ 4 = 30 cm.

solution.say: Find the turning effect on the left: the force times its distance from the pivot.
The right side must have the same turning effect. Divide by the 4 N force.
The 4 N weight must hang 30 cm to the right of the pivot.

items.prompt: Workers push the same heavy box into a truck. Which ramp needs the smallest push?

options.text: a short ramp with a steep slope
options.why: A steep ramp needs a bigger push, even though the distance is shorter.

options.text: no ramp: lifting the box straight up
options.why: Lifting straight up needs the biggest force, equal to the box's whole weight.

options.text: a long ramp with a gentle slope

options.why: Sand adds friction, which makes pushing harder.

hints: A ramp lets you raise a load a little at a time.
A gentler slope spreads the lift over a longer distance.
Compare a gentle ramp with lifting the box straight up.
items.explanation: A long, gentle ramp needs the smallest push, but you must push the box further. Simple machines trade a smaller force for a longer distance.

items.prompt: A pulley system lets a builder lift a 400 N load with an effort of only 100 N. How many metres of rope must the builder pull to lift the load by 1 m?
hints: A machine that makes your force smaller makes you move further.
Compare the load with the effort: how many times smaller is the effort?
Multiply the 1 m lift by that number.
items.explanation: The effort is 4 times smaller than the load, so the rope must be pulled 4 times as far. To lift the load 1 m, the builder pulls 4 m of rope.

items.prompt: Label the parts of this lever.

figure.alt: A long flat plank rests on a small triangle under its middle. A square block sits on the left end. A downward arrow points at the right end.

hints: Tap a label, then tap its number.
The load is the thing you want to move.
The pivot is the fixed point that the lever turns on.
items.explanation: The lever turns on the pivot. The block on the left is the load, and the arrow shows the effort pushing down on the right.

items.prompt: Workers must raise a crate to the same height using one of these ramps. Tap the ramp that needs the smallest effort force.

figure.alt: Three ramps labelled A, B and C stand side by side on the ground. All three rise to the same height. Their lengths along the ground are different.

hints: A longer, gentler slope needs less push but a longer distance.
All three ramps reach the same height.
Find the ramp with the longest sloping surface.
items.explanation: Ramp C is the longest and the gentlest. You push over a longer distance, so you need a smaller force.

items.prompt: A lever balances on a pivot. A 40 N weight hangs 30 cm to the left of the pivot. Another weight hangs 20 cm to the right. How heavy must the right weight be?
hints: For balance, force × distance on the left equals force × distance on the right.
Work out force × distance for the left side first.
Left side: 40 × 30. Divide it by 20 to find the right weight.
items.explanation: Left side: 40 N × 30 cm = 1200. Right side: weight × 20 cm must also be 1200, so the weight is 60 N.

items.prompt: Maya balances a 5 N weight 24 cm from the pivot with an 8 N weight on the other side. How far is the 8 N weight from the pivot?
hints: The turning effects on both sides must be equal.
Multiply the first weight by its distance.
5 × 24 = 120. Which distance times 8 gives 120?
items.explanation: 5 N × 24 cm = 120. For 8 N to give 120 it needs to be 120 ÷ 8 = 15 cm from the pivot.

items.caption: A lever kept balanced
items.prompt: Leo kept a lever balanced and changed the effort and its distance from the pivot. Complete the table.
head: Effort (N)
Distance from pivot (cm)
hints: The effort times the distance stays the same every time.
Multiply the numbers in the first row.
60 × 10 = 600. Find what × 40 gives 600, and 10 × what gives 600.
items.explanation: Effort × distance is always 600. At 40 cm the effort is 15 N, and for an effort of 10 N the distance is 60 cm.

items.prompt: Gear A has 12 teeth and turns clockwise. Its teeth mesh with gear B, which has 36 teeth. Compared with gear A, how does gear B turn?

options.why: A bigger gear is slower and meshing gears turn in opposite directions.
Gears that mesh push each other the opposite way round.
The gear with more teeth turns more slowly.

hints: Meshing gears turn in opposite directions.
The gear with more teeth goes round fewer times.
B has three times as many teeth as A.
items.explanation: Meshing gears turn opposite ways. B has more teeth, so it makes fewer turns than A and turns more slowly.

items.prompt: Gear A has 15 teeth and turns 12 times. It drives gear B, which has 20 teeth. How many times does gear B turn?
hints: Count the total teeth that pass the meeting point.
In 12 turns, gear A moves 12 × 15 teeth past that point.
Divide the total number of teeth by the 20 teeth on gear B.
items.explanation: Gear A moves 12 × 15 = 180 teeth. Gear B has 20 teeth, so it turns 180 ÷ 20 = 9 times.

items.prompt: Dimas pushes a barrel up to a platform 1 m high. He can use a ramp 2 m long or a ramp 4 m long. What is the difference?

options.text: The 4 m ramp needs a smaller push, but he pushes over a longer distance.
The 4 m ramp needs a bigger push but a shorter distance.
options.why: A longer ramp is gentler, so it needs a smaller push.

options.text: Both ramps need the same push, because the height is the same.
options.why: The slope is different, so the force is different.

options.text: The 4 m ramp needs less push and a shorter distance.
options.why: There is no ramp that makes you push less over a shorter path.

hints: A gentle slope is easier to push up.
What do you give up when the ramp is longer?
Compare the force and the distance for each ramp.
items.explanation: A longer ramp is gentler, so it needs a smaller force. The cost is that the barrel must move a longer distance.

items.prompt: A 120 N crate must be raised 0.5 m using a smooth ramp that is 2 m long. Ignoring friction, what effort force is needed?
hints: The ramp trades distance for force.
Work done lifting straight up equals force × height.
120 × 0.5 = 60. Share that over the 2 m of ramp.
items.explanation: Lifting straight up takes 120 × 0.5 = 60 (N × m). Over 2 m of ramp the effort is 60 ÷ 2 = 30 N.

items.prompt: Sort these tools and objects by the type of simple machine they use.
hints: A lever turns around a pivot.
A ramp is a slope and a pulley uses a rope over a wheel.
Start with the objects that have a rope.
items.explanation: A crowbar, scissors and a bottle opener turn on a pivot. A slope is a ramp. A rope over a wheel is a pulley.

items.prompt: All these ramps rise to the same height. Order them from the one needing the least effort to the one needing the most.
hints: A longer ramp is gentler.
Gentler slopes need less effort.
Start with the longest ramp.
items.explanation: For the same height, a longer ramp needs less force. So the 8 m ramp needs the least and the 2 m ramp needs the most.

items.prompt: Match each part of a lever to its meaning.
pairs: the fixed point the lever turns on
the force you apply to the lever
a bar that turns on a pivot
hints: The word load means something heavy to carry.
Which part stays still while the bar turns?
You supply the effort.
items.explanation: The pivot does not move. You apply the effort, the load is moved and the bar is the lever.

items.prompt: Sekar says: "A lever lets me do the same job with a smaller force, so it saves me from doing any work." What is the best reply?

options.text: She is right, because the force is smaller so the job is easier in every way.
options.why: The force is smaller but there is a cost.

options.text: She is wrong, because levers need a bigger force.
options.why: A lever can reduce the force you need.

options.text: She is partly right: the force is smaller, but she moves her end a longer distance.
She is wrong, because levers only work with a pulley.
options.why: A lever works on its own with a pivot.

hints: Think about the long end of a see-saw.
What do you gain and what do you give up?
Compare how far each end of the lever moves.
items.explanation: A lever can make the force smaller, but the end you push moves a longer distance. The job is easier to do, not free.

items.prompt: Rangga uses a crowbar to lift a rock. Choose 2 changes that make the job easier.

options.text: Move the pivot closer to the rock
Push down further from the pivot
Push down closer to the pivot

hints: The bigger the distance from the pivot to the effort, the smaller the force you need.
Think about which distance you want longer and which shorter.
Make the effort distance longer or the load distance shorter.
items.explanation: Moving the pivot nearer the rock shortens the load side. Pushing further from the pivot lengthens the effort side. Both mean less force.

items.prompt: A wheel with teeth that fits into another wheel with teeth is called a ___.
hints: Bicycles use these to turn the back wheel.
They are in clocks and machines.
Its name starts with the letter g.
items.explanation: A wheel with teeth is a gear. Meshing gears pass on movement.

items.prompt: A lever turns on a fixed point called the ___. The force you apply is the ___, and the thing being moved is the ___.
hints: Each gap names a different part of the lever.
The effort is what you provide.
The first gap is the point the bar turns around.
items.explanation: A lever turns on a pivot. You apply the effort to move the load.

items.prompt: Putri measured the effort needed to pull a 20 N trolley up to the same height on ramps of different lengths. What does her evidence suggest about a 6 m ramp?

options.text: It will need no effort at all.
options.why: Friction and the trolley's weight still need some effort.

options.text: It will need more than 8 N, because longer ramps are harder.
options.why: The table shows longer ramps need less effort.

options.text: It will need less than 4.5 N, but still more than 0 N.
It will need exactly 4.5 N, the same as the 4 m ramp.
options.why: The effort keeps falling as the ramp gets longer.

hints: Look at the trend in the table as the ramp gets longer.
The effort falls, but is there a limit?
Compare the 4 m effort with what a 6 m ramp would probably need.
items.explanation: The effort falls as the ramp gets longer, so a 6 m ramp should need less than 4.5 N. It can never reach zero because the trolley still has weight and friction.

items.prompt: A wheelbarrow carries heavy soil. It is a lever. Where is its pivot?

options.text: At the handles where you lift.
options.why: The handles are where you apply the effort.
The soil is the load.

options.text: At the axle of the wheel at the front.
At the legs at the back.
options.why: The legs rest on the ground but are not the pivot.

hints: The pivot is the point the lever turns around.
When you lift the handles, what stays on the ground?
Think about the wheel at the front.
items.explanation: When you lift the handles, the barrow turns around the wheel axle at the front. That makes the axle the pivot.

items.prompt: True or false: A seesaw is a kind of lever.
hints: What is the middle called?
It turns about a point.
A lever has a pivot.
items.explanation: A lever is a bar that turns around a fixed point called a pivot.

items.prompt: True or false: A ramp makes a job easier because you do less work in total.
hints: Is the path longer?
Is the force smaller?
It needs less force over more distance.
items.explanation: A ramp lets you use a smaller force over a longer distance. The effort is easier but the total work is not smaller.

items.prompt: True or false: A pulley changes the direction of the force you pull.
hints: Which way do you pull?
Which way does the load go?
It changes direction.
items.explanation: With a pulley at the top, you pull down to lift something up.

items.prompt: True or false: Two gears that touch turn in the same direction.
hints: Look at two cogs.
One goes clockwise.
They turn opposite ways.
items.explanation: Meshing gears turn in opposite directions.

items.prompt: A lever turns about a fixed point called the ___.
hints: The see-saw has one in the middle.
It is the turning point.
It starts with p or f.
items.explanation: The pivot (or fulcrum) is the point a lever turns about.
